findings.evidence: Lines 600-618: the private lemma's hypotheses are `{g : E → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, g x < ∞)` with all Haar/normed instances omitted; the public wrapper's body is `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top hM`. Mathlib has the opposite direction public and no `eLpNorm_toReal` (grep `eLpNorm_ofReal`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Basic.lean:443).
findings.fix: Delete `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq` and make `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top` public (it needs only `[MeasurableSpace E]`, per its own `omit`, so state it outside the `Haar` section); if the general lemma is to stay unexposed, keep it `private` and drop the wrapper, calling it directly in `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal`.
findings.issue: `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq` is public but is a pure instantiation of the private `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top` (proof is `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top hM`, adding no maximal-function content), used only inside `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal`. The general lemma — the actual reusable statement, and the dual of Mathlib's public `eLpNorm_ofReal` — is the one hidden, so the exposure is inverted and the surface carries two names for one fact.

findings.evidence: `maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` (line 169) is unconditional; `ae_maximalFunction_lt_top_of_eLpNorm_ne_top` handles `rcases eq_or_ne p ∞ with rfl | hp_top` at lines 584-586 using exactly that bound.
findings.fix: Drop `hp_top` from `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top` and `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal`, splitting on `p = ∞` and closing that branch with `maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` + `eLpNorm_exponent_top` (the same two steps already used at lines 585-586).
findings.issue: `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal` requires `hp_top : p ≠ ∞`, and `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top` (line 573) likewise, although both hold at `p = ∞`: `eLpNorm (maximalFunction μ f) ∞ μ = essSup (maximalFunction μ f) ≤ eLpNormEssSup f μ ≠ ∞`. The companion `ae_maximalFunction_lt_top_of_eLpNorm_ne_top` deliberately covers `p = ∞`, so that generality has no consumer and the flagship `MemLp` result silently omits an endpoint the file develops.

summary: The reusable content of the new eLpNorm-preservation result is private while a contentless maximal-function specialization of it is public, and both new finiteness lemmas exclude p = ∞ although the file's own L^∞ endpoint gives that case immediately.
